name: Deepa Jewellers Ltd
tagline: Newly-listed (Sept 2026) Hyderabad-based B2B gold jewellery supplier to South-India retail chains, with exceptional headline ratios (56% ROE, 52% ROCE, 38% revenue growth) - this pass confirms a clean compliance record (no litigation, no auditor concerns) but quantifies a real supplier-concentration risk (top 10 karigars/suppliers = 91.81% of purchases) and thin operating margin (8% OPM), with a company-disclosed in-house manufacturing facility underway to address exactly that dependency.
business_overview: Deepa Jewellers Limited (incorporated 2016, converted to a public company Sept 2025) is an organised B2B designer, processor and supplier of hallmarked gold jewellery, based in Hyderabad, serving jewellery retail chains and standalone stores exclusively across South India (no direct-to-consumer sales). Promoters Ashish Agarwal, Seema Agarwal and Dev Agarwal have 24+ years in gems and jewellery. The company sources gold/silver via RBI-registered banks, bullion dealers and the India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX), then supplies raw materials to a network of 41 third-party karigars (artisans) who process and return finished, hallmarked ornaments - an outsourced manufacturing model. IPO listed NSE/BSE Sept 8, 2026 at ~25% premium to its Rs 177 issue price; net fresh-issue proceeds (~Rs 250 Cr) are earmarked ~Rs 215 Cr for long-term working capital (inventory scaling) and the balance for general corporate purposes. Seeded 2026-09-13 via untrusted X triage (@JakeraChoudhury, bullish, very-high conviction).

fundamentals_narrative: This deep-dive pass largely confirms and quantifies the risks the original write-up flagged qualitatively, without surfacing any new red flag: the DRHP and post-listing disclosures show no litigation pending against the company, its promoters, directors, KMPs or senior management, and no auditor qualifications/reservations/adverse remarks (auditor: NSVR & Associates LLP) - a clean compliance record. The 'no demonstrated moat, commodity-like B2B trading' caution from the original pass is now quantified concretely: the top 10 of the company's 41 karigars/suppliers account for 91.81% of purchases, a real concentration risk in an outsourced-manufacturing model where the company itself doesn't directly control production. Operating margin is thin (8% OPM FY26), consistent with bullion-trading economics where gold cost dominates COGS. FY26 operating and free cash flow were both negative (-Rs 15 Cr and -Rs 19 Cr) as the business scaled inventory and borrowings rose (Rs 81 Cr -> Rs 117 Cr) - a real cash outflow, though less concerning than in other sectors given gold inventory itself carries monetisable/collateral value rather than being sunk work-in-progress. Constructively, the company is already addressing the karigar-concentration risk: an in-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad (6,696 sq ft, with 3D wax printers, vacuum pressure casting machines and induction melting furnaces) is under construction, expected operational around H1 FY27/Sept 2026 (sources vary on the exact date), explicitly aimed at reducing third-party dependency, improving quality control and margin, and cutting pilferage risk.

verdict_headline: Strong, consistent headline growth (38% revenue, accelerating PAT) with a confirmed clean compliance record - but this pass quantifies a real supplier-concentration risk (91.81% via top 10 karigars) and thin operating margin, while the track record remains only ~8 days of public trading. four_box score of 3.5 would technically permit a growth label, but is still not applied given the short history. thesis_fit 'neither' (analyst override, unchanged), conviction reaffirmed Medium.

four_box unchanged at 3.5 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation yes); thesis_fit remains 'neither' (analyst_override) - the track record is still far too short (~8 days of trading, one disclosed FY) to responsibly apply a 10x/100x label regardless of the otherwise-attractive numbers.
